Egyptian composer [Hesham Nazih](/wiki/Hesham_Nazih "Hesham Nazih") had composed the score for the series by early March 2022 in his first major English language project.[[98]](#cite_note-DiabInterviewMar2022-98)[[123]](#cite_note-Nazih-123) He used an orchestra of 62 musicians and 36 singers,[[124]](#cite_note-VarietyMCUComposers-124) which were recorded at [Synchron Stage Vienna](/wiki/Synchron_Stage_Vienna "Synchron Stage Vienna"),[[125]](#cite_note-SynchronStage-125)[[124]](#cite_note-VarietyMCUComposers-124) while soloists playing Egyptian folk instruments such as the [arghul](/wiki/Arghul "Arghul"), [mizmar](/wiki/Mizmar_(instrument) "Mizmar (instrument)"), and [rebab](/wiki/Rebab "Rebab") were recorded in Cairo. Nazih felt the folk instruments had a "prominent presence and sonority" within the score and did not work against the "texture" of the classical orchestra.[[124]](#cite_note-VarietyMCUComposers-124) Diab was drawn to Nazih to score the series because his work "encompasses authentic Egyptian elements in a very contemporary way",[[28]](#cite_note-DiabTHRApr2022-28) with the music helping to break Egyptian stereotypes by revealing some of the country's lesser-known [contemporary art](/wiki/Contemporary_art_in_Egypt "Contemporary art in Egypt") to international audiences; Diab described it as a "beautiful score that is Egyptian, but it's international at its core, it's universal".[[58]](#cite_note-DiabEgyptPitch-58) Naz

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f0/Independence_Hall_Assembly_Room.jpg/250px-Independence_Hall_Assembly_Room.jpg)](/wiki/File:Independence_Hall_Assembly_Room.jpg)

The Assembly Room at [Independence Hall](/wiki/Independence_Hall "Independence Hall") in [Philadelphia](/wiki/Philadelphia "Philadelphia"), where the [Second Continental Congress](/wiki/Second_Continental_Congress "Second Continental Congress") adopted the [Declaration of Independence](/wiki/United_States_Declaration_of_Independence "United States Declaration of Independence")

Throughout the first half of 1776, Adams grew increasingly impatient with what he perceived to be the slow pace of declaring independence.[[73]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESmith1962a263-75) In the [Second Continental Congress](/wiki/Second_Continental_Congress "Second Continental Congress") in Philadelphia, he helped push through a plan to outfit armed ships to launch raids on enemy vessels. Later in the year, he drafted the first set of regulations for the provisional navy.[[74]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcCullough200199–100-76) Adams drafted the preamble to the [Lee Resolution](/wiki/Lee_Resolution "Lee Resolution") of colleague [Richard Henry Lee](/wiki/Richard_Henry_Lee "Richard Henry Lee").[[75]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMaier199837-77) He developed a rapport with delegate [Thomas Jefferson](/wiki/Thomas_Jefferson "Thomas Jefferson") of Virginia, who had been slower to support independence but by early 1776 agreed that it was necessary.[[76]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcCullough2001113–117-78) On June 7, 1776, Adams [seconded](/wiki/Second_(parliamentary_procedure) "Second (parliamentary procedure)") the Lee Resolution, which stated that the colonies were "free and independent states."[[77]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFerling1992146-79)

[Federalism grants substantial autonomy](/wiki/Federalism_in_the_United_States "Federalism in the United States") to the 50 states. **Alaska** ([/əˈlæskə/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English") [ⓘ](/wiki/File:En-us-Alaska.ogg "File:En-us-Alaska.ogg") [*ə-LASS-kə*](/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key")) is a [non-contiguous](/wiki/Non-contiguous_United_States "Non-contiguous United States") [U.S. state](/wiki/U.S._state "U.S. state") located in the northwestern regions of [North America](/wiki/North_America "North America"). Part of the [Western United States](/wiki/Western_United_States "Western United States") region, it is one of the two non-contiguous U.S. states, alongside [Hawaii](/wiki/Hawaii "Hawaii"). Alaska is considered to be the northernmost, westernmost, and, longitudinally, the easternmost state in the [United States](/wiki/United_States "United States").[[a]](#cite_note-6) It is a [semi-exclave](/wiki/Enclave_and_exclave "Enclave and exclave") of the U.S., bordering the [Canadian territory](/wiki/Provinces_and_territories_of_Canada "Provinces and territories of Canada") of [Yukon](/wiki/Yukon "Yukon") and the [province](/wiki/Provinces_and_territories_of_Canada "Provinces and territories of Canada") of [British Columbia](/wiki/British_Columbia "British Columbia") to the east. It shares a western [maritime border](/wiki/Maritime_boundary "Maritime boundary") in the [Bering Strait](/wiki/Bering_Strait "Bering Strait") with [Russia](/wiki/Russia "Russia")'s [Chukotka Autonomous Okrug](/wiki/Chukotka_Autonomous_Okrug "Chukotka Autonomous Okrug"), and is closer to another continent ([Asia](/wiki/Asia "Asia")) than any other U.S. state. The [Chukchi](/wiki/Chukchi_Sea "Chukchi Sea") and [Beaufort](/wiki/Beaufort_Sea "Beaufort Sea") Seas of the [Arctic Ocean](/wiki/Arctic_Ocean "Arctic Ocean") lie to the north, and the [Pacific Ocean](/wiki/Pacific_Ocean "Pacific Ocean") to the south.

Alaska is the [largest U.S. state by area](/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_area "List of U.S. states and territories

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2f/Neptune%2C_Earth_size_comparison_true_color.jpg/250px-Neptune%2C_Earth_size_comparison_true_color.jpg)](/wiki/File:Neptune,_Earth_size_comparison_true_color.jpg)

A size comparison of Neptune and Earth

Neptune's mass of 1.024×1026 kg[[8]](#cite_note-fact-10) is intermediate between Earth and the larger [gas giants](/wiki/Gas_giant "Gas giant"): it is 17.15 times that of Earth but just 1/19th [that of Jupiter](/wiki/Jupiter_mass "Jupiter mass").[[g]](#cite_note-mass-85) Its [gravity](/wiki/Gravity "Gravity") at 1 bar is 11.27 m/s2, 1.15 times the [surface gravity](/wiki/Surface_gravity "Surface gravity") of Earth,[[8]](#cite_note-fact-10) and surpassed only by Jupiter.[[79]](#cite_note-Unsöld_&_Baschek_2001-86) Neptune's [equatorial](/wiki/Equator "Equator") radius of 24,764 km[[11]](#cite_note-Seidelmann_Archinal_A'hearn_et_al._2007-13) is nearly four times [that of Earth](/wiki/Earth_radius "Earth radius"). Neptune, like [Uranus](/wiki/Uranus "Uranus"), is an [ice giant](/wiki/Ice_giant "Ice giant"), a subclass of [giant planet](/wiki/Giant_planet "Giant planet"), because they are smaller and have higher concentrations of [volatiles](/wiki/Volatile_(astrogeology) "Volatile (astrogeology)") than Jupiter and Saturn.[[73]](#cite_note-Boss-79) In the search for [exoplanets](/wiki/Exoplanet "Exoplanet"), Neptune has been used as a [metonym](/wiki/Metonymy "Metonymy"): discovered bodies of similar mass are often referred to as "Neptunes",[[80]](#cite_note-87) just as scientists refer to various extrasolar bodies as "Jupiters".

In 1966, Charles spent two terms at the [Timbertop](/wiki/Timbertop "Timbertop") campus of [Geelong Grammar School](/wiki/Geelong_Grammar_School "Geelong Grammar School") in Victoria, Australia, during which he visited Papua New Guinea on a school trip with his history tutor, Michael Collins Persse.[[24]](#cite_note-powedu-31)[[25]](#cite_note-32) Charles later described his time at Timbertop as the most enjoyable part of his education.[[26]](#cite_note-33) On returning to Gordonstoun, he became [head boy](/wiki/Head_boy "Head boy"), and left in 1967 with six [GCE O-levels](/wiki/GCE_O-levels "GCE O-levels") and two [A-levels](/wiki/A-level "A-level") in history and French, at grades B and C respectively.[[24]](#cite_note-powedu-31)[[27]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrandreth2007145-34) Reflecting on his schooling, Charles later remarked that he "didn't enjoy school as much as I might have", adding that he was "happier at home than anywhere else".[[23]](#cite_note-Colditz_kilts-30)

fanoutqa_003461.t: Alexander I of Russia :: Emperor :: War of the Sixth Coalition :: part 02 :: chunk_0016
fanoutqa_003461.x:
Alexander I of Russia :: Emperor :: War of the Sixth Coalition :: part 02 :: chunk_0016
Alexander sent an envoy to meet with the French to hasten the surrender. He offered generous terms to the French and although having intended to avenge Moscow,[[46]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMontefiore2016313-50) he declared himself to be bringing peace to France rather than its destruction. On 31 March[[47]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMaude1911223-51) [Talleyrand](/wiki/Charles_Maurice_de_Talleyrand "Charles Maurice de Talleyrand") gave the key of the city to the tsar. Later that day the Coalition armies triumphantly entered the city with Alexander at the head of the army followed by the King of Prussia and Prince Schwarzenberg. Until this battle it had been nearly 400 years since [a foreign army had entered Paris](/wiki/History_of_Paris#Plague_and_war "History of Paris"), during the [Hundred Years' War](/wiki/Hundred_Years%27_War "Hundred Years' War").

On 2 April, the [Sénat conservateur](/wiki/S%C3%A9nat_conservateur "Sénat conservateur") passed the *[Acte de déchéance de l'Empereur](/wiki/Acte_de_d%C3%A9ch%C3%A9ance_de_l%27Empereur "Acte de déchéance de l'Empereur")*, which declared Napoleon deposed. Napoleon was in [Fontainebleau](/wiki/Fontainebleau "Fontainebleau") when he heard that Paris had surrendered. Outraged, he wanted to march on the capital, but his [marshals](/wiki/Marshal_of_the_Empire "Marshal of the Empire") refused to fight for him and repeatedly urged him to surrender. He abdicated in favour of his son on 4 April, but the Allies rejected this out of hand, forcing Napoleon to abdicate unconditionally on 6 April. The terms of his abdication, which included his exile to the Isle of [Elba](/wiki/Elba "Elba"), were settled in the [Treaty of Fontainebleau](/wiki/Treaty_of_Fontainebleau_(1814) "Treaty of Fontainebleau (1814)") on 11 April. A reluctant Napoleon ratified it two days later, marking the end of the War of the Sixth Coalition.
